correctness.rationale: For each of the five symbol-multiplicity partitions, the five legal swap actions give explicit ball-size profiles. Packing-count inequalities bound each component (one, two, two, three, four); the nontrivial four-ball candidate in (2,1,1) would require exactly the four size-three centers, two of which share outputs. The five displayed codes have pairwise disjoint balls and attain every ceiling. Symbol relabeling and component summation yield the polynomial for every integer \(q\ge2\). Standalone exhaustive verification checks every canonical center, all 43023 forbidden superoptimal subsets, and global code constructions for \(q=2,\ldots,6\); finite checking is corroborative and no unproved infinite extrapolation is asserted.

value.rationale: Determines the next natural short-block exact correcting capacity after the known three-coordinate case, uniformly for all alphabets; establishes five sharp symbol-multiplicity packing obstructions and constructions, not merely a routine binary reproduction. The strictly positive gap \(qA_q(3;1)-A_q(4;1)=q^2(q-1)(q-2)/6\) for \(q\ge3\) quantifies a real finite-block synchronization penalty and yields optimal message counts at q=3,4,5,... . No asymptotic theorem is claimed.
